# Chatbot design for customer support

Curated by Skill Harbor — @asgard-ai-platform's cs-chatbot-design skill, listed here with credit to its creator: a practical guide to designing customer-support chatbots that actually resolve tickets instead of enraging callers. It covers intent taxonomies (how to map the real reasons customers contact support), conversation-flow design (happy paths, disambiguation, slot-filling), escalation triggers and human-handoff patterns (when the bot must quit gracefully), brand tone and guardrails, grounding in knowledge bases, multilingual and accessibility considerations, and evaluation (containment rate, CSAT, escalation quality, A/B testing). Honest caveats: it's a design guide, not a deployable bot — your chat platform (Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, or a custom build) and its billing are yours; it won't write your intent training data for you; and no chatbot design survives first contact with real customers unchanged — the skill treats evaluation and iteration as part of the design. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
